question: A home-insurance renewal letter, worded the way many were. Which line is where staying put cost Britons billions?
answer: The price, quietly raised because you stayed. Britain's competition regulator put the cost of loyalty at about £4 billion a year across five markets in 2018. The insurance regulator's name for it was price walking, and from 2022 it banned charging renewing home and motor customers more than new ones.
move: Check what a newcomer would pay before renewing anything.
ask: Which of my contracts renewed itself this year without my comparing the price?

scene.title: Your renewal
scene.body: Thank you for being a valued customer. Your policy will renew automatically. Your new premium reflects our latest pricing. No action is needed.

phrases.plain: customer we expect not to compare
phrases.why: Staying is read as a sign you won't compare. That is worth money to the insurer.

phrases.plain: renew at our new price unless you stop it
phrases.why: Doing nothing counts as yes. The default does the selling.

phrases.plain: is higher, partly because you stayed
phrases.why: Regulators called it price walking: a little more each year for those who never left.
The best price usually goes to whoever asks. Silence is the profitable answer.

scene.ask: One phrase is where loyal customers pay. Which?
scene.watch: A letter that asks you to do nothing is asking for the highest price.
